articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a telescope mirror grinding demonstration for Astronomy Day at the Tech Museum of Innovation. Members meticulously showcased the initial stages of crafting a Pyrex mirror, from grinding a spherical curve with abrasives to preparing it for polishing with a pitch lap. The event provided an engaging, hands-on experience for attendees, serving as a unique educational outreach for astronomy.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities calendar for June, July, and August, 1999. It details multiple star parties at various locations like Houge Park, Fremont Peak, and Pinnacles National Monument, as well as general meetings with guest speakers. The calendar also includes observational astronomy classes covering topics such as object identification and basic astrophotography.

articles.title: Astronomy Day at The Tech
articles.summary: The article recounts a two-day Astronomy Day event at The Tech museum where nearly 200 visitors participated in grinding and polishing a telescope mirror and assembling a new telescope. This 'Signature' scope, signed by all participants, was successfully tested on distant objects and the Moon, impressing observers with its clarity. The telescope will be added to the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner program, demonstrating that a functional telescope can be built in a short period.

articles.title: Short-lived Lunar Views: The Lassell Stripe
articles.summary: During a star party on April 24, Akkana Peck and David North observed an unusual dark, straight line near the Straight Wall on the Moon, initially mistaking it for a Transient Lunar Phenomenon (TLP) due to its absence in some atlases and its short visibility. Subsequent research using more detailed atlases and historical drawings by Harold Hill and T.S. Elger identified the feature as 'Rima Lassell' or the 'Lassell stripe', a fault traversing an oval-shaped ring, which is only visible under very specific lighting conditions.

articles.title: Meteor Watch
articles.summary: This article details the South Delta Aquarids meteor shower in July, noting that its primary peak is best viewed from the Southern Hemisphere and is hindered by a full moon for Northern Hemisphere observers. However, it highlights a weaker, earlier peak from the northern branch of the shower's double radiant that aligns with a new moon, offering better viewing opportunities for those in the North. The article indicates that combined activity in late July can reach 30 meteors per hour under dark skies, marking the beginning of summer meteor observing.

articles.title: Minutes of the Meeting of the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The Board of Directors meeting addressed various administrative and operational items, including the unanimous appointment of Mark Taylor as treasurer and the approval of guidelines for email voting on non-financial matters. Key discussions involved planning future events like the auction/swap meet, Astronomy Day, and star parties, as well as improving the quality and print quantity of "The Ephemeris" publication. Additionally, the board established a cooperation agreement with the Fremont Peak Observatory Association for star parties and worked on internal organizational tasks such as creating an officer duty list and soliciting designs for an official SJAA logo.

articles.title: Apollo 11 Commemoration Set
articles.summary: A ceremony is scheduled for July 24, 1999, on the USS Hornet at NAS Alameda to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the Apollo 11 splashdown. Astronauts Buzz Aldrin and Alan Bean are confirmed attendees, with Bean exhibiting his lunar art, alongside other dignitaries, solar telescopes from Chabot Observatory, and a NASA display of Apollo items.

articles.title: Dave North
articles.summary: The article outlines various celestial events for the month, highlighting opportunities to observe both the new and full moons. It details techniques for spotting the new crescent moon shortly after 'new' and describes a minor partial lunar eclipse, along with an excellent chance to view the Mare Orientale on the moon's western limb due to favorable libration. Additionally, a tight grouping of the Moon, Venus, and Regulus is noted as a 'pseudo' event.

articles.title: SETI@Home with SJAA
articles.summary: The SETI@Home project rapidly gained half a million participants in its first month, leading to server difficulties and a data shortage where users unknowingly processed duplicate data. New equipment donations and data flow are anticipated to resolve these issues. The article encourages readers to join the SJAA group within the competitive SETI@Home community.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for the month of July, detailing the visibility and key features of various planets. Mars is receding but still observable, while Jupiter is returning to the night sky. Venus offers a dynamic view as its phase changes and it reaches greatest brilliancy, with tips for daytime observation. Additionally, Neptune reaches opposition, Uranus is well-placed, and Saturn is visible in the morning sky, alongside Earth's aphelion.

articles.title: About SJAA Star Parties
articles.summary: The article describes three primary star party locations hosted by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA): Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, and Fremont Peak State Park. It highlights the unique features of each, such as sky quality, visitor recommendations, and types of observing experiences available, catering to both beginners and experienced deep-sky observers. The SJAA also provides a hotline for directions to these events.

articles.title: Seeing Stardust - A Deep Sky Project for the Novice
articles.summary: This article introduces a deep sky observing project for novices, focusing on the Sagittarius Star Cloud and the Galactic Center in July. It guides observers to locate the "Teapot" asterism within Sagittarius and introduces the concept of dark nebulae as starlight-obscuring matter. A specific target for observation is highlighted: dark nebula Barnard 86 (B-86) alongside the open cluster NGC 6520.

articles.title: Continued from Page 7
articles.summary: The article describes Barnard's Ink Spot (B86), a prominent dark nebula in Sagittarius, detailing its appearance as a distinct inky spot against the Milky Way. It provides practical tips for amateur astronomers to locate B86 using low power, wide-field telescopes, and star-hopping techniques from celestial markers like Gamma Sagittarii or M8. The text also mentions other dark nebulae, such as those within the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae, and highlights their significance as primordial matter for future stars.

articles.title: Summer Star Parties at Pinnacles
articles.summary: Pinnacles National Monument is expanding its nighttime visitor programs with "Pinnacles Starry Nights," offering astronomical viewing, talks, and light pollution awareness. They are seeking amateur astronomers from the San Jose Astronomical Association to help. The program's 1999 dates include July 16, August 13, September 11, October 2, and November 17, often coinciding with new moons or meteor showers.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: The article reports on a recent increase in faint comet discoveries, predominantly by automated asteroid and comet search programs like LINEAR and LONEOS, with mentions of Comets Lee, LINEAR (1998 T1), and Tempel 2. It then delves into the high percentage of "accidental" visual comet discoveries in the Southern Hemisphere, discussing potential reasons such as comets being outside typical hunting areas, rapid brightening, or increased activity from non-dedicated comet hunters, facilitated by the internet and awards.

articles.title: Ephemerides
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemeris data for three comets: C/1999 H1 (Lee), C/1998 T1 (LINEAR), and Periodic Comet Tempel 2 (P/55). For each comet, it lists celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elevation, sky visibility (evening or morning), and estimated visual magnitude at 5-day intervals from early June to mid-August. This data is essential for astronomers and observers to locate and track these celestial objects.

articles.title: Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a compilation of orbital elements for three celestial objects: Lee, LINEAR (T1), and P/Tempel 2. For each object, detailed astronomical data such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period are provided. This information serves as ephemeris data, likely for the tracking and observation of these comets or minor planets.

articles.title: Mike Koop
articles.summary: Lick Observatory has announced the 1999 season dates for its popular Music of the Spheres and Summer Visitors Program, with tickets available through the UCSC Box Office and expected to sell out quickly. The Music of the Spheres program, held on New Moon weekends, features concerts, lectures by prominent astronomers like Alex Filippenko and Steve Vogt, and viewing through the 36" telescope, while the Summer Visitor's Program on First Quarter Moon weekends offers lectures and viewing through both the 36-inch and 40-inch telescopes. Additionally, a challenge pledge is underway to raise $25,000 for 36" dome renovation, to be matched by the Barkley Foundation.

articles.title: July 1999
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for July 1999, detailing lunar phases, the positions and magnitudes of Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, along with their rise, transit, and set times. It also includes information on hours of darkness, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights a 'Darkest Saturday Night' for optimal observing.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and Board of Directors for an organization, providing their names, roles (President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, Directors), and respective contact phone numbers. It serves as a directory for the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document lists the staff members and their contact information for 'Ephemeris Staff'. It identifies Jane Houston and Morris Jones as editors, Bob Brauer and Lew Kurtz for circulation, and Accuprint for printing services, along with their respective phone numbers.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris is inviting its members to submit articles for publication. Interested members should send their contributions directly to the editors via email at ephemeris@whiteoaks.com.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article announces that all loaner telescopes are currently available to members of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association). Members interested in borrowing a scope should contact Mike Koop via email or phone, providing both work and home numbers.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The article lists telescopes, referred to as "Stored Scopes," that are available for immediate loan to members of the SJAA. These scopes are kept at the homes of other SJAA members, and interested borrowers should contact Mike Koop to arrange pick-up at a listed SJAA event.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document provides a list of telescopes currently loaned out, detailing each scope's description, the borrower, and its due date. It also informs readers that those interested in borrowing a scope can be placed on a waiting list until it becomes available after its return date.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists astronomical telescopes that have had their loan periods extended, making them available for future borrowing through coordination with the current user. It provides details on specific scopes, their current borrowers, and due dates where applicable. Interested individuals are encouraged to contact the organization to arrange a transfer.

articles.title: Waiting List:
articles.summary: The document presents a "Waiting List" that is currently empty. It indicates that there are no entries for scope descriptions or borrowers at this moment.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly throughout the year. The document also provides mailing list subscription and unsubscription instructions for the newsletter.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing fees for standard and junior memberships, with an option to add a Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for payment via check payable to SJAA and submission either at a meeting or by mail to their P.O. Box in Campbell, CA. The form also requests personal contact information from applicants.
